content.text:
I've confirmed the direction of every MFN-type provision. Findings:

- **p0031 (§ 7.6)** — MFN runs *in our favour*: "Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer..." This benefits us; not to be flagged or redlined.
- **p0051 (§ 12.3)** — express negative covenant confirming we owe no most-favoured-customer commitment.
- No reverse-MFN anywhere in Fees (§ 7), Term/Renewal (§ 8), Customer Responsibilities (§ 12), Publicity (§ 25), or General (§ 30); targeted searches for "no less favourable", "most-favoured", "favourable terms third party", "benchmark", "exclusive supplier", and "first refusal" surfaced only the two paragraphs above.

input.quote: Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: The agreement imposes no MFN obligation on us, which is the preferred position. Section 12.3 (p0051) expressly records that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment, and no other provision requires us to extend Vendor our best terms or to match a third-party offer (checked Fees § 7, Term and Renewal § 8, Customer Responsibilities § 12, Publicity § 25 and General § 30, plus targeted searches for "no less favourable", "most-favoured", "benchmark", "exclusive supplier" and "first refusal"). The only MFN in the document, § 7.6 (p0031), runs in our favour: Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms. Per the rule's direction guidance, a Vendor-granted MFN benefiting the Customer is welcome and is not redlined. No change requested.

mappings.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
mappings.quote: Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
